verses.1: On Saturday, he was carried around by the people who were playing games with him. His disciples also felt the seeds as they rubbed them against their hands.
verses.2: And some of the Pharisees said, “What is wrong with this, that it isn’t suitable for Sabbaths?”
verses.3: And when Jesus answered them, he said, “Do you not understand this? This is what David did when he was arrested by the authorities, along with those who were with him.”
verses.4: Just as he entered the house of God and ate the offerings that were prepared for Him, so too did he give those who were with him to eat. But these people weren’t allowed to eat those offerings, unless they were priests alone.
verses.5: And he said to them: “The Lord is the Son of Man.”
verses.6: On another Sabbath, he went to the assembly to teach others. There was a man there, and his right hand was dry.
verses.7: But the officials and the Pharisees wondered whether he actually healed on the Sabbath, so that they could accuse him of breaking the law.
verses.8: He, however, knew how to conduct those discussions himself. He said to the man who had a dry hand, “Stand up and come to the middle.” Then he stood up.
verses.9: And Jesus said to them, “I ask you, whether it is right for you to do good or evil on the Sabbath day, to save lives or to destroy them.”
verses.10: And looking at them all, he said to him, “Stretch out your hand.” So he did, and his hand was stretched out.
verses.11: But they became proud, and they discussed with each other what they should do to Jesus.
verses.12: On those same days, he was encouraged to go up to the mountain. During his night-time prayers to God, he did just that.
verses.13: And when the day came, he called his disciples together. From among them, he selected twelve men, whom he called apostles.
verses.14: Simon, who was also called Peter, and his brother Andrew, as well as James, John, Philip, and Bartholomew.
verses.15: And Mathai, Thomas, and Jacob from Helfa’u, and Simon, who was also called Zilot.
verses.16: And Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor.
verses.17: And you stood with them in a open place. A large crowd of students gathered around him. There was also a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, the coast of Tyre, and Sidon.
verses.18: Those who came to hear him and to be healed from their diseases. And those who suffered from foul breath were also cured.
verses.19: And all the crowd wanted to be able to see him, because a power came from him, and it affected everyone.
verses.20: And he also put his eyes on his disciples, saying, “It is better for the poor, because it is true that the kingdom of God belongs to them.”
verses.21: Those who suffer now are fortunate, for they will be rewarded. Those who cry now are fortunate, for they will laugh in the end.
verses.22: It will be fortunate when people hate you. And when they oppress you, they will also praise and call your name a “evil one” because of the son of man.
verses.23: Thank you on that day, and may you be blessed. For indeed, your reward in heaven is great. This is what their ancestors also did for their prophets.
verses.24: But also to you, the rich ones, because you refuse to answer your calls.
verses.25: Do not you, who are now surrounded by troubles, think that you will be able to escape them? Do not you, who are now laughing, think that you will be able to live without sorrow and suffering?
verses.26: When everyone else speaks to you properly, then it’s because their fathers also did the same thing to those false prophets.
verses.27: But I say to those who listen, love your enemies. Treat those who hate you well.
verses.28: Praise those who have suffered for your sake, and pray for those who are being persecuted by you.
verses.29: Take the other one as well when you go to the saria. And do not cover your shirt and pants with your cloak.
verses.30: Please be patient and give in to their demands. And from that point on, don’t demand anything more than what they can offer.
verses.31: And just as you want people to do for you, do the same for them.
verses.32: And even if you love those who love you, what kind of grace is that for you? For indeed, the sinners will also love those who love them.
verses.33: And if you do good to those who do good to you, what kind of favor is that? The wicked also do the same thing.
verses.34: And if you lend money to someone in the hope of getting it back, what kind of favor is that for you? And sinners will only lend money to other sinners, so that they can get their own debts paid off.
verses.35: Also, love your enemies, do good to them, and don’t give them anything in return. The reward you will receive will be great. You will be considered children of high status, because it is beneficial for those who are hated and evil.
verses.36: Be you the householders, just as your father is the householder.
verses.37: And do not judge, nor be judged. And do not condemn, nor be condemned. Let go of things that are already over, and let them be over.
verses.38: Give it to them, and it will be given to you. They will give you a good measure, carefully measured and prepared, to be placed in your possession. For with a measure, you will be measured, and they will be measured against you.
verses.39: He also made a parable for them: Can a blind person possibly guide another blind person? Neither can they get out of the ditch together.
verses.40: A student cannot be better than the teacher; instead, everyone should be treated as if they were the teacher himself.
verses.41: And how can you see the pupil in your brother’s eye, when you don’t understand what the cornea is in your own eye?
verses.42: How can you say that to your brother? Brother, I’ll remove the lens in your eye. Will he still be able to see through your eyes? Pretend first that you’ve removed the lens from your own eye. Then, you’ll be able to see the lens in your brother’s eye as well.
verses.43: It’s not possible to make a good tree by creating bad fruit; nor can one make good fruit by creating a bad tree.
verses.44: For each tree, it grows from its own fruit. They do not collect grapes from grapes, nor do they pick ivy from trees.
verses.45: The good person speaks the good from the treasure of goodness in his heart. The wicked person, on the other hand, speaks evil from their own evil nature. In fact, due to an excess of goodness in their hearts, their mouths speak evil.
verses.46: What do you call me? Lord, please don’t do what I say.
verses.47: Every one who approaches me, and hears my words and acts according to them, I will show you what kind of person he is.
verses.48: One who builds a house with great effort and care, and lays the foundation stone on the rock, is truly like a person who has built a house. But when a flood occurs, the river flows over that house. He cannot prevent it from being destroyed because he built it poorly.
verses.49: And he who heard this and did not build a house on the earth, without having laid the foundation, was destroyed by the river. Soon after, the river rushed over him, and his house became completely destroyed.
